subject: Revised-Romanization spelling of the vowel ㅡ across all course data

sources: korean/data/*.json (excluding app-data.json, which is generated by scripts/build-app-data.mjs)
scope.note: app-data.json and public/data/* are build outputs; they pick these corrections up on rebuild and were not edited by hand.

method.rule: In Revised Romanization the vowel ㅡ is always spelled `eu`. ㅢ is `ui` and is excluded.

passes.name: count
passes.detail: Decompose each Korean string, count syllables whose jungseong index is 18 (ㅡ, not 19/ㅢ), and compare against the number of `eu` occurrences in the paired romanization.

passes.name: onset
passes.detail: For every ㅡ syllable with a real consonant onset (not ㅇ), require <onset>+`eu` to appear. Immune to the cross-syllable `eu` artifact, so it catches an error even when a spurious `eu` elsewhere would have balanced the count pass.

passes.name: artifact-discounted count
passes.detail: Re-run the count pass after discounting `eu` substrings provably produced by a coda-less ㅐ/ㅔ/ㅚ/ㅙ/ㅞ/ㅒ/ㅖ syllable followed by 우 or 의 (매우 maeu, 새우 saeu, 회의 hoeui). Closes the one channel that can hide a u-for-eu error.

method.falseLeadRejected: An early pass discounted every `eu` immediately followed by `i`, on the theory that `eui` was an alternate ㅢ spelling. That is wrong: in ㅡ+이 sequences (체크인 chekeuin, 로그인 rogeuin, 쓰이다 sseuida, 포스트잇 poseuteuit) the `eu` is a genuine ㅡ and the `i` belongs to the next syllable. The rule manufactured 68 false positives and was dropped.
method.adjudication: Every surviving candidate was read by hand. Only entries judged genuinely misspelled were changed.

fixes.reason: 노트 is `noteu`; the ㅌ+ㅡ syllable was dropped entirely. Every other occurrence in the corpus already spells it `noteu` (noteu jom billyeojul…, noteubuk), so this was the lone outlier.

The 는 alternant carries a ㅡ and was unromanized. The repo's own convention for the identical pattern shape spells both branches: .entries[125] `V-(eu)n/neunde`, .entries[62] `-(eu)n/neun semida`, .entries[68] `-(eu)n/neun pyeonida`.
Same defect, second occurrence: the explanation quotes the romanization inline, so leaving it would have contradicted the corrected field one key above.

Surfaced by the ㅡ pass because 오늘 (oneul) was missing, but the field was broken more broadly: it romanized only the last word, spelled 죠 as `jo`, and ended in a period for a question. 죠 is `jyo` everywhere else in the corpus, including the near-identical 오늘 밖에 많이 춥죠? → `oneul bakke mani chupjyo?`. Judgment call: fixing the flagged ㅡ was impossible without restoring the dropped words.
ㅃ+ㅡ spelled with bare `u`. chapter-35 already spells the same stem correctly as `bappeunde-yo`.
적 + 으로 liaises to [저그로]; the 으 is `geu`, not `gu`.

fixes.before: daedanhaneyo. suibi jureodleulkka bwa geokjeongdoejin anayo?
fixes.after: daedanhaneyo. suibi jureodeulkka bwa geokjeongdoejin anayo?
fixes.reason: 들 mis-split as `dleul` instead of `deul`. Only the onset pass caught this one: the stray `leul` supplied an `eu` that balanced the count pass, so it was invisible to a naive /eu/ tally.
The 는 syllable (neun, a ㅡ) was dropped from 모르는데요. Sibling examples in the same note spell it out: `meogeonneunde-yo`, `inneunde-yo`.
궁금 is `gunggeum`; the second ㅡ was spelled `u`. chapter-14 already has the correct `gunggeumhan`.

못 흘려요 → mo teullyeoyo (못 coda ㄷ + ㅎ → ㅌ)
간접흡연 → ganjeopeubyeon (접 coda ㅂ + ㅎ → ㅍ)
dismissed.verdict: Correct. The romanization follows actual pronunciation, so the ㅡ is spelled keu/teu/peu rather than heu. This is the sound-change exception, not an error.

dismissed.class: romanization field carrying an English gloss
examples: N + 수 + 단위 (세는 말) → "noun + number + counter"
dismissed.verdict: Not romanizations. These grammar.json entries use the field for a descriptive label, so there is nothing to correct.
Correct. The parenthetical is a Korean definition, not part of the term being romanized.

dismissed.class: ㅡ followed by 이 (script artifact, not a data defect)
dismissed.verdict: Correct. Flagged only by the rejected `eui` rule described under method.falseLeadRejected.

dismissed.class: ㅇ-onset ㅡ after a vowel-final syllable
dismissed.verdict: Correct. The `eu` is preceded by a vowel letter but is a genuine ㅡ.

dismissed.class: hyphenated romanization mistaken for an artifact
dismissed.verdict: Correct. Hyphenation means no spurious `eu` substring ever forms; the artifact discount over-fired.

outOfScopeObservations.what: Neighbouring lines in the same dialogue carry non-ㅡ romanization slips: 놀랐어요 → `nollaasseoyo` (doubled a), 마음먹었어요 → `maeumeogeosseoyo` (dropped m), 할게요 → `eungwonhalkkeyo` (kk for g).
